knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.2.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly links expectation of a function, covariance, and correlation for a joint distribution?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Joint expectation weights g by joint probabilities or density. Covariance captures linear co-movement, while correlation standardises it.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: E[g]=sum or integral of g times joint; Cov=E[XY]-EX EY; Corr=Cov/(SDX SDY).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Assuming zero covariance proves independence or reversing correlation standardisation.

choices.label: E[g(X,Y)] is the sum or integral of g(x,y) weighted by the joint distribution. Cov(X,Y)=E[XY]-E[X]E[Y], and Corr(X,Y)=Cov(X,Y)/(SD(X)SD(Y)).
E[g(X,Y)] is found from marginal means alone for every g, so the joint distribution is unnecessary.
Correlation equals covariance multiplied by both standard deviations, so it retains measurement units.
Covariance measures all forms of dependence, and zero covariance proves independence for any joint distribution.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.2.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. P(0,0)=0.2, P(0,1)=0.3, P(1,0)=0.1, P(1,1)=0.4. Which covariance statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Compute E[X], E[Y], E[XY], and covariance.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Only cell (1,1) contributes to E[XY]. Subtracting the product of the means gives 0.05.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Assuming independence from marginals or using E[XY] as covariance without centring.

choices.label: E[XY]=E[X]E[Y]=0.35 by definition, so covariance must be zero before checking the joint table.
Cov(X,Y)=E[XY]=0.4 because covariance is the expected product without centring.
E[X]=0.5 and E[Y]=0.7 imply independence, so no E[XY] calculation is needed.
